$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identities that correspond to the following trigonometric identities:

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},\,\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x},\,\operatorname{csch}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{coth}⁡x{csch}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x})}^{2}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{sinh}^{3}⁡x}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x.$ Then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x.$

| $x$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡2$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ |

Now, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{sinh}^{3}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3/4}^{4/3}\frac{1}{{u}^{3}}\,\cdot \text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{3/4}^{4/3}{u}^{-3}\,\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{u}^{-3+1}}{-3+1}\,{|}_{3/4}^{4/3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{u}^{2}}\,{|}_{3/4}^{4/3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2}}+\frac{1}{2{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{9}{32}+\frac{8}{9} \\  & =\frac{175}{288}\end{aligned}
$$
